note: Demo seed assessment content. Scores indicate recall of the concepts tested here and are not a professional certification of competence.

assessments.title: Python Fundamentals
assessments.description: Core syntax, built-in types, functions and error handling.

questions.question: What is the output of len('SkillBridge')?
questions.explanation: 'SkillBridge' has 11 characters, and len() on a string returns its character count.

questions.question: Which type does 7 / 2 evaluate to in Python 3?
questions.explanation: The / operator always performs true division and returns a float, so 7 / 2 is 3.5.

questions.question: Which of these creates a dictionary?
questions.explanation: Curly braces with key: value pairs create a dict; {1, 2, 3} would create a set.

questions.question: What is the result of bool([]) ?
questions.explanation: Empty containers are falsy in Python, so bool([]) is False.

questions.question: Which keyword defines an anonymous function?
questions.explanation: lambda creates a small anonymous function inline, e.g. lambda x: x + 1.

questions.question: What does a try/except block do?
options: Handles exceptions that occur in the try block
questions.correct_answer: Handles exceptions that occur in the try block
questions.explanation: try/except catches exceptions raised during execution of the try block so the program can recover.

questions.question: What is the value of 'abc'.upper()?
questions.explanation: .upper() returns a new string with all characters in upper case; strings are immutable.

questions.question: Which statement about tuples is correct?
questions.explanation: A tuple cannot be changed after creation, unlike a list.

questions.question: What does range(3) produce when iterated?
questions.explanation: range(3) starts at 0 and stops before 3, yielding 0, 1, 2.

questions.question: Which syntax correctly opens a file and guarantees it is closed?
questions.explanation: The with statement acts as a context manager and closes the file even if an error occurs.

assessments.title: JavaScript Essentials
assessments.description: Types, scope, arrays, functions and asynchronous behaviour.

questions.question: Which keyword declares a block-scoped variable that cannot be reassigned?
questions.explanation: const declares a block-scoped binding that cannot be reassigned (though object contents can still change).

questions.question: What does typeof '5' return?
questions.explanation: typeof reports the type of the value; '5' is a string literal.

questions.question: What does [1, 2, 3].map(n => n * 2) return?
questions.explanation: map returns a new array containing the result of the callback for each element.

questions.question: What is the result of 1 == '1' ?
questions.explanation: == performs type coercion, so '1' is converted to 1. === would compare without coercion and give false.

questions.question: Which method removes the last element from an array?
questions.explanation: pop() removes and returns the final element; shift() removes from the front.

questions.question: What does a Promise represent?
options: An eventual result of an asynchronous operation
questions.correct_answer: An eventual result of an asynchronous operation
questions.explanation: A Promise settles to either a resolved value or a rejection reason in the future.

questions.question: Which declaration creates a function?
questions.explanation: function declarations use the function keyword. Function expressions assigned to variables are also valid.

questions.question: What does JSON.parse('{"a":1}') return?
questions.explanation: JSON.parse converts a JSON string into a JavaScript value, here an object.

questions.question: What is the value of undefined ne null ?
questions.explanation: undefined and null are loosely equal, so undefined == null is true (undefined === null is false).

questions.question: How do you refer to the object a method was called on in an arrow function?
options: You cannot; arrow functions do not bind their own 'this'
questions.correct_answer: You cannot; arrow functions do not bind their own 'this'
questions.explanation: Arrow functions capture 'this' lexically from the enclosing scope rather than binding their own.

assessments.title: React Fundamentals
assessments.description: Components, props, state, hooks and rendering behaviour.

questions.question: What is JSX?
options: A syntax extension that looks like HTML inside JavaScript
questions.correct_answer: A syntax extension that looks like HTML inside JavaScript
questions.explanation: JSX is compiled into function calls that create React elements.

questions.question: Which hook adds local state to a function component?
questions.explanation: useState returns the current value and a setter that triggers a re-render.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the dependency array in useEffect?
options: It controls when the effect re-runs
questions.correct_answer: It controls when the effect re-runs
questions.explanation: The effect re-runs when any listed dependency changes; an empty array runs it once after mount.

questions.question: How is data passed from a parent to a child component?
questions.explanation: Props are read-only inputs a parent passes down to a child.

questions.question: Why does React need a 'key' prop when rendering a list?
options: To identify which items changed, were added or removed
questions.correct_answer: To identify which items changed, were added or removed
questions.explanation: Keys let React reconcile lists efficiently and preserve element state correctly.

questions.question: What does the useEffect cleanup function do?
options: Runs before the effect re-runs or the component unmounts
questions.correct_answer: Runs before the effect re-runs or the component unmounts
questions.explanation: The returned function releases resources such as subscriptions and timers.

questions.question: Which statement about props is correct?
options: Props are mutable inside the child
questions.explanation: A child must not mutate its props; it communicates upward using callbacks.

questions.question: When does a component re-render?
options: When its state or props change
questions.correct_answer: When its state or props change
questions.explanation: React schedules a re-render when state or props change, or when a parent re-renders.

questions.question: What is the best way to share state between distant components?
options: Lifting state up or using context
questions.correct_answer: Lifting state up or using context
questions.explanation: Lifting state to a common ancestor or using context keeps data flow explicit and predictable.

questions.question: What is a controlled input?
options: An input whose value is driven by React state
questions.correct_answer: An input whose value is driven by React state
questions.explanation: Its value comes from state and updates via onChange, making React the single source of truth.

assessments.title: SQL and Relational Queries
assessments.description: SELECT, joins, aggregation, constraints and indexing.

questions.question: Which clause filters rows before grouping?
questions.explanation: WHERE filters individual rows before aggregation; HAVING filters after grouping.

questions.question: What does an INNER JOIN return?
options: All rows from the left table
Only rows with a match in both tables
questions.correct_answer: Only rows with a match in both tables
questions.explanation: INNER JOIN keeps only the rows where the join condition matches in both tables.

questions.question: Which statement removes all rows but keeps the table structure?
questions.explanation: TRUNCATE removes all rows quickly and keeps the table; DROP removes the table itself.

questions.question: What is a primary key?
options: A column that may contain duplicates
A column or set of columns uniquely identifying each row
questions.correct_answer: A column or set of columns uniquely identifying each row
questions.explanation: A primary key enforces uniqueness and is never null.

questions.question: Which function counts non-null values in a column?
questions.explanation: COUNT(column) counts non-null values; COUNT(*) counts rows.

questions.question: What does a foreign key enforce?
options: That a value references an existing row in another table
questions.correct_answer: That a value references an existing row in another table
questions.explanation: Referential integrity prevents orphaned references to rows that do not exist.

questions.question: Which index structure does PostgreSQL create by default?
questions.explanation: PostgreSQL defaults to B-tree indexes, which support equality and range queries.

questions.question: What is normalization primarily for?
options: Reducing data redundancy and update anomalies
questions.correct_answer: Reducing data redundancy and update anomalies
questions.explanation: Normal forms remove duplicated data so a single change is recorded in one place.

questions.question: Which JOIN returns all left rows plus matches from the right?
questions.explanation: LEFT JOIN preserves every left row, filling unmatched right columns with NULL.

questions.question: What does LIMIT 10 do combined with ORDER BY score DESC?
questions.explanation: ORDER BY sorts descending and LIMIT keeps the first 10 rows of that order.

assessments.title: Git and Version Control
assessments.description: Commits, branches, merging and collaboration workflow.

questions.question: Which command records staged changes as a new commit?
questions.explanation: git commit creates a snapshot of the currently staged changes.

questions.question: What does git clone do?
options: Copies a remote repository locally with its history
questions.correct_answer: Copies a remote repository locally with its history
questions.explanation: git clone downloads the repository and checks out the default branch.

questions.question: What is a merge conflict?
options: When Git cannot automatically combine overlapping changes
questions.correct_answer: When Git cannot automatically combine overlapping changes
questions.explanation: Git marks the conflicting regions and requires a human to choose the correct result.

questions.question: Which command shows the commit history?
questions.explanation: git log lists commits in reverse chronological order.

questions.question: What does git pull do?
options: Fetches remote changes and merges them into the current branch
questions.correct_answer: Fetches remote changes and merges them into the current branch
questions.explanation: git pull is fetch followed by merge (or rebase, if configured).

questions.question: What is a branch in Git?
options: A copy of the whole repository
A movable pointer to a commit
questions.correct_answer: A movable pointer to a commit
questions.explanation: Branches are lightweight pointers, which is why switching is fast.

questions.question: Which file lists paths Git should ignore?
questions.explanation: Patterns in .gitignore exclude files such as build output and secrets from tracking.

questions.question: What does git stash do?
questions.explanation: stash saves work in progress so you can switch context, then restore it later.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a pull request?
options: To propose and review changes before merging
questions.correct_answer: To propose and review changes before merging
questions.explanation: A pull request enables review, discussion and checks before changes land on the target branch.

questions.question: Which command creates and switches to a new branch?
questions.explanation: The -b flag creates the branch and checks it out in one step (git switch -c also works).

assessments.title: Docker Containers
assessments.description: Images, containers, volumes, networking and Compose.

questions.question: What is the difference between an image and a container?
options: An image is a template; a container is a running instance of it
A container is stored on disk; an image runs
questions.correct_answer: An image is a template; a container is a running instance of it
questions.explanation: A container adds a writable layer on top of an immutable image.

questions.question: Which instruction sets the base image in a Dockerfile?
questions.explanation: FROM must be the first instruction (after comments and ARG) and defines the starting image.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a volume?
options: To persist data outside the container lifecycle
questions.correct_answer: To persist data outside the container lifecycle
questions.explanation: Data written to a volume survives container removal and rebuilds.

questions.question: What does EXPOSE 8000 in a Dockerfile do?
options: Publishes the port to the host
Documents the port the container listens on
questions.correct_answer: Documents the port the container listens on
questions.explanation: EXPOSE is documentation; publishing requires -p or the ports key in Compose.

questions.question: Why copy requirements.txt before the application source?
options: So the dependency layer is cached and reused when only source changes
questions.correct_answer: So the dependency layer is cached and reused when only source changes
questions.explanation: Docker caches layers; keeping dependencies in an earlier layer avoids reinstalling them on every code edit.

questions.question: What does docker compose do?
questions.explanation: Compose describes services, networks and volumes in YAML and manages their lifecycle together.

questions.question: What is the CMD instruction for?
options: Providing the default command a container runs
questions.correct_answer: Providing the default command a container runs
questions.explanation: CMD sets the default executable and arguments, which can be overridden at run time.

questions.question: What does ADD or COPY do?
questions.explanation: COPY copies from the build context; ADD additionally handles URLs and archives.

questions.question: A container can reach another by name in Compose. Why?
options: Compose provides service-name DNS on a shared network
questions.correct_answer: Compose provides service-name DNS on a shared network
questions.explanation: Services on the same Compose network resolve each other by service name.

questions.question: What is a multi-stage build used for?
options: Keeping the final image small by discarding build-only tooling
questions.correct_answer: Keeping the final image small by discarding build-only tooling
questions.explanation: Each FROM begins a stage; only the artefacts needed at runtime are copied into the final stage.

assessments.title: Machine Learning Foundations
assessments.description: Supervised learning, evaluation, overfitting and data splitting.

questions.question: What is supervised learning?
questions.explanation: Supervised models learn a mapping from inputs to known target labels.

questions.question: What is overfitting?
options: The model performs well on training data but poorly on unseen data
questions.correct_answer: The model performs well on training data but poorly on unseen data
questions.explanation: The model has memorised noise specific to the training set rather than the underlying pattern.

questions.question: Why is a test set kept separate from training data?
options: To estimate performance on unseen data
questions.correct_answer: To estimate performance on unseen data
questions.explanation: Evaluating on data the model never trained on gives an honest performance estimate.

questions.question: Which metric suits a heavily imbalanced binary classification?
questions.explanation: With rare positives, accuracy is misleading because predicting the majority class scores highly.

questions.question: What does cross-validation provide?
options: A more reliable performance estimate across multiple splits
questions.correct_answer: A more reliable performance estimate across multiple splits
questions.explanation: k-fold cross-validation averages results over k train/validation splits, reducing variance of the estimate.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a validation set?
questions.explanation: The validation set guides choices; the test set is reserved for the final unbiased estimate.

questions.question: Which is a regression task?
options: Predicting whether an email is spam
questions.explanation: Regression predicts a continuous value, unlike classification which predicts a category.

questions.question: What does regularisation do?
questions.explanation: L1/L2 penalties discourage large coefficients, improving generalisation.

questions.question: What is data leakage?
options: Information from the test set influencing training
questions.correct_answer: Information from the test set influencing training
questions.explanation: Leakage produces optimistic results that do not hold in production, e.g. scaling before splitting.

questions.question: Which is an unsupervised task?
questions.explanation: Clustering finds structure without target labels, so it is unsupervised.
